reason: The main open issue is the data incident. Our own email (event-013) sent another tenant's name, address, rent arrears amount and payment arrangement to Iris. She still holds it and asks what to do with it (event-014, event-020). The Privacy Lead has not recorded an assessment or notification decision (event-017, event-018). Arrears are a never-touch topic and need a person, so I did not tell Iris to delete or keep it on my own authority. I staged an update that asks her to keep it for now and not share it. This is a pending decision for the privacy team and property manager, so waiting or asking the tenant would not resolve it. The damp job is secondary. Iris reports a darker stain but no dripping, heat, sparks or tripped breaker, so there is no reported danger (event-009, event-020). It is not P0 and urgent_by_code is false. Iris reports no health impact and no vulnerable occupant, so it is not P1. The inspection missed its 6 March slot because of a breakdown, and Owen offered 7 March after 13:00, subject to confirmation (event-019). The owner approved the inspection fee only, and nothing intrusive is approved (event-011). I did not instruct Brindle to rebook. The handover lists confirming 7 March, which is inspection-only and covered by event-011, as an option once Iris confirms. The address check flag is only a formatting difference (short form against the full address), not a mismatch. Priority is P2 because of the privacy clock and the missed appointment, not because of any danger.

actions.body: Dear Iris, thank you for your message. The contractor could not attend today because of a vehicle breakdown, so the inspection did not take place. He has offered tomorrow, 7 March, after 13:00, and we are not yet able to confirm it. Could you let us know whether you can be home then? On the earlier email, please do not forward or share it, and please keep it for now. Our privacy lead is reviewing it, and we will tell you what to do with it as soon as we can. If the stain spreads quickly, you notice any dripping, or you see heat, sparks or a tripped breaker near the socket, please tell us straight away. Kind regards, Maya Chen, Northbridge Lettings
